land.text: Harrien, Wierland and Reval, which asked for Swedish protection in June 1561, and Jerwen somewhat later

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Livonian Conference row ends in 1563; the Teutonic Order bought Estonia from Denmark in 1346.

land.text: Estonia: the Estonian nobility and Reval capitulated on 29 September (O.S.) / 10 October (N.S.) 1710; Russian hegemony was formalised by the Peace of Nystad in 1721

successors.note: Cliopatria has the Tsardom of Russia to 1720 and the Russian Empire from 1721.

capitals.name: Reval (Tallinn)
capitals.note: The page names no capital; Reval is the main city, the seat of the lord lieutenant and later the governor under the Swedish Governors-General.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row (its Kingdom of Sweden shape adds northern Estonia only in 1564, the Swedish Empire from 1612). June 1561: 'Harrien (Harjumaa), Wierland (Virumaa) and Reval (Tallinn) asked for and received Swedish protection from King Eric XIV'. Narva was Russian from 1558. The page gives no area.
New keyframe: Jerwen (Järvamaa) came 'somewhat later' than June 1561; the page gives no year and 1562 is a bridging reading.

correction.text: the same with Narva and eastern Wierland (Ida-Viru), retaken 1581

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Sweden had retaken Narva in 1581' (Livonian War page); Russia had held Narva since 1558. The page says Narva and Ivangorod stayed under Swedish control in 1583; Ivangorod lies across the Narva river in Ingria and belongs to the swedish-ingria dossier.

correction.text: the Duchy of Estonia of 1583: the northern parts and Dagö (Hiiumaa)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'in 1583 the northern parts and Dagö (Hiiumaa) were under Swedish control, and the Duchy of Estonia was created from this territory'; the Treaty of Plussa (10 August 1583) confirmed Narva. Wiek (Lääne) is not on the page for these years.

correction.text: northern Estonia with Wiek (Läänemaa): all of present-day Estonia was Swedish in 1645 (southern Estonia and Ösel in Swedish Livonia)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Brömsebro (1645) 'Sweden therefore controlled all of present-day Estonia, including Ösel'. The page does not say when Wiek (Läänemaa) became Swedish, so it is added in 1645 as a bridging reading (confidence 1); southern Estonia and Ösel belong to swedish-livonia.

ledger.note: June 1561: northern Estonia places itself under Sweden. 'Harrien (Harjumaa), Wierland (Virumaa) and Reval (Tallinn) asked for and received Swedish protection from King Eric XIV'; Swedish rule runs 'between 1561 and 1710'.
1562: Jerwen (Järvamaa) follows. The page says it came 'somewhat later' than June 1561; the year 1562 is a bridging reading, not the page's.

1581: Sweden retakes Narva. 'Sweden had retaken Narva in 1581'; Narva and Ivangorod stayed under Swedish control in the Treaty of Plussa (10 August 1583), which the Swedish Estonia page also notes ('Sweden kept the territory that had sought its protection and captured Narva'). Ivangorod, across the river, is left to the swedish-ingria dossier; only Narva and Ida-Viru are drawn here.
1583: the Duchy of Estonia is created from the northern parts and Dagö, under Swedish control. Same state, same colour.
1583: Dagö (Hiiumaa) is Swedish. The page says only that 'the northern parts and Dagö were under Swedish control' in 1583; it does not say who held Dagö before or how Sweden got it.

region.text: Wierland and Jerwen: Wesenberg (Rakvere) and Weissenstein (Paide)

ledger.note: 1602: Polish-Lithuanian forces fight in Swedish Estonia. Chodkiewicz 'defeated a Swedish relief force at Wesenberg (Rakvere)' by 1602 and beat the Swedish generals at Weissenstein (Paide) in 1604; Reval, Pernau and Narva stayed Swedish. The page says Sweden had 'taken control of Estonia and most of Livonia' in 1600.
1611: a truce after the death of Charles IX ends the war; the infobox gives 'status quo ante bellum', so Swedish Estonia is unchanged.

1645: Wiek (Läänemaa) is counted in Swedish Estonia. The page: 'Under the Peace Treaty of Brömsebro, the island of Saaremaa (Ösel) was ceded by Denmark to Sweden. Sweden therefore controlled all of present-day Estonia'; the page names Wiek nowhere and the Livonian War page has Denmark holding Hapsal, Leal and Lode, so the year is bridging.

29 September (O.S.) / 10 October (N.S.) 1710: Reval and the Estonian nobility capitulate to Russia. 'The Estonian nobility and the city of Reval capitulated on 29 September 1710 (O.S.) / 10 October 1710 (N.S.)'; Swedish Estonia page: 'The war on Estonian territory ended with the capitulation of Tallinn in September 1710'. The capitulation confirmed Danish-era law and the privileges of the German nobles.
1710: Swedish rule in Estonia ends. 'Russian hegemony was formalized in 1721, through the Peace of Nystad.'

wars.name: Livonian War
wars.outcome: Sweden kept the lands that had sought its protection in 1561 and held Narva (retaken 1581); the Treaty of Plussa of 10 August 1583 left Narva and Ivangorod with Sweden and Russia gave up most of Ingria.
wars.note: The Swedish Estonia page dates the treaty 1583 as ending the Livonian War.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1600-1611)
wars.outcome: Status quo ante bellum; Reval, Pernau and Narva remained Swedish through the war; truce 1611.
wars.note: Dorpat's recapture is April 1603 on one line and 1604 on another.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: The war on Estonian soil ended with the capitulation of Reval in September/October 1710; Russia was confirmed by the Peace of Nystad in 1721.
wars.note: Reval capitulated 29 September 1710 O.S., 10 October N.S.

certainty.note: Drawn from county names, which only approximate the medieval Harrien, Wierland, Jerwen and Wiek; the page gives no boundary or area. Narva's frontier with Ivangorod is a river line.

sources.title: Swedish Estonia
sources.note: 1561-1710, June 1561 protection, 1583 Plussa and the Duchy of Estonia, 1629 and 1645, 1710 and 1721.

notes: Type colony: a dominion of the Swedish crown (the page: governed by a lord lieutenant, later a governor, under the Swedish Governors-General). Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sweden shape contains northern Estonia from 1564 and its Swedish Empire shapes from 1612; the renderer should draw this as a tint of Sweden, not a separate colour. Four pages opened. Not settled: when Jerwen came (page: 'somewhat later'), who held Dagö before 1583 and when Wiek became Swedish (pages silent; both entered at confidence 1), the Narva-Ivangorod frontier. Reval's capitulation is 29 September O.S. on one page and 'September 1710' on the other; the dossier uses the N.S. month (10). Southern Estonia (Dorpat, Fellin, Pernau) and Ösel are in swedish-livonia, not here; the 1561 Estonia/Livonia line follows the old county names. Swedish Ingria and Kexholm are separate states needing dossiers (swedish-ingria is in this batch). Review eu-14-x (2026-10-31): counterpart kingdom-of-denmark (Cliopatria row 936-1406) replaced by denmark-norway for the 1583 and 1645 events and the Livonian War.
